translations.text: The proverbs of Solomon, son of David, who reigned over Israel,
for knowing wisdom and instruction, and for understanding words of insight,
for receiving subtle turns of speech, and for knowing righteousness and truth, and for setting judgment right;
so that it may give knowledge to the innocent, and understanding and discernment to young children;
by hearing these the wise will become wiser, and the one who has knowledge will gain guidance;
he will understand a parable and a hidden saying, the sayings of the wise and their riddles.
The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord; there is good understanding for all who practice it, and devotion to God is the beginning of knowledge. The ungodly despise wisdom and instruction.
Listen, my son, to your father's instruction, and do not reject your mother's law.
For you will set a crown of grace on your head, and a golden necklace around your neck.
My son, do not let ungodly men lead you astray, and do not want to go with them, even if they plead with you and say to you:
"Come with us and share in bloodshed, and let us deceitfully thrust a righteous man down into the earth,
and let us swallow him alive as Hades swallows, and wipe out the memory of him from the earth.
And let us seize his very fruitful property, and fill our houses with plunder.
Cast in your lot with us, and let all of us together acquire a common pavasik [?] (purse?), and let us have one vashkaran [?] (pouch?)."
My son, do not walk on the road with them; turn your feet away from their paths.
For it is not in vain that a snare is spread for a bird.
For those who are guilty of murder store up evils for themselves, and the overthrow of lawless men is wretched.
These are the ways of all who commit lawlessness, for they destroy their own souls.
Wisdom is praised in the streets, and she moves openly in the squares;
she is proclaimed from the tops of the walls, she takes her stand at the gates of the mighty, and at the gates of the city she speaks boldly:

"As long as the innocent hold to righteousness, they will not be ashamed. But the foolish, who are eager for insolence, have become ungodly; they have hated knowledge and have become accountable to knowledge.
Look, I will set before you the sayings of my spirit, and I will teach you my words.
For I called you, and you did not listen to me; I spoke at length, and you paid no attention to me;
instead you despised my counsels and took no notice of my rebukes.
So now I in turn will laugh at your destruction, and I will rejoice when distress and siege come upon you."
And when turmoil comes upon you suddenly, and ruin comes like a whirlwind, or when destruction falls upon you,
for it will be that when you call on me, I will not listen to you. The wicked will seek me and will not find me,
because they hated wisdom and did not seek the fear of the Lord.
They did not even want to heed my counsels, and they despised my rebukes.
From now on they will eat the fruit of their own way and be filled with their own ungodliness.
This is because they wronged the little ones and killed them, and judgment destroyed the ungodly.
But whoever listens to me will dwell in hope and will rest without fear of any evil.
My son, if you receive the commandments spoken by my soul and hide them within you,
and your ear pays attention to wisdom, and you set them before your son as a sign, and give your heart to understanding;
if you call out, and lift your voice to wisdom and understanding,
and if you seek it like silver and search it out like treasure,
then you will understand the fear of the Lord and find the knowledge of God.
For the Lord gives wisdom, and from his mouth come knowledge and understanding.
He stores up life, and he helps those who walk uprightly on their way,
guarding the paths of righteousness, and he guards the way of those who fear him.
Then you will understand righteousness and judgment, and every good path will be made straight.
If wisdom comes into your mind and knowledge into your soul, you will find pleasure in doing good.
Good counsel will guard you, and a holy mind will keep you,
to deliver you from the evil way and from the man who speaks what cannot be trusted.
Woe to those who have left the straight ways and walked in the ways of darkness,
who rejoice over wickedness and delight in evil perversity,
whose ways are crooked and whose paths are perverse,
so as to lead you away from the straight way and make you a stranger to a righteous mind.
My son, do not let evil counsel overtake you, the evil counsel that abandons the teaching of youth and forgets the divine law.
For she has set up her house beside death, and her paths lead down into hell, to the ones born of the earth.
None of those who walk in her will return. Instead they will be sorry, and they will not reach the paths of uprightness, for the years of life will not reach them.
If they had been perfect in the paths of good, they would have found the paths of righteousness straight,
for the upright will inherit the earth, and the holy will remain on it.
But the ways of the ungodly will be destroyed from the earth, and the lawless will go out from it.
My son, do not forget my law, and let your heart keep my words,
for length of days and years of life will be added to you.
Do not let mercy and faithfulness be lacking in you. Bind them around your neck, and you will find grace.
Plan ahead what is good before God and before people.
Trust in God with all your heart, and do not be lifted up by your own wisdom.
In all your ways know him, so that he may make your ways straight and you will not strike your foot.
Fear the Lord, and turn away from all evil.
Then there will be healing for your flesh and care for your bones.
Honour the Lord from your righteous labours, and offer him the first of your righteous fruits,
so that you may be filled with plenty of wheat, and your winepresses will overflow with wine.
My son, do not lose heart under the Lord's discipline, and do not grow weak when he rebukes you,
for the Lord teaches the one he loves, and he punishes every son he accepts.
Blessed is the man who has found wisdom, and the mortal who has seen understanding,
for she is better to gain than treasures of gold and silver.
She is more precious than precious carbuncles. Nothing resists her, not a single evil thing. She is also plain to all who come near her. Nothing precious is equal to her,
for length of days and years of life are in her right hand, and in her left hand are glory and riches.
Righteousness comes out of her mouth, and she carries law and mercy on her tongue.
Her ways are good ways, and all her paths are in peace.
She is a tree of life to all who accept her, and to those who rely on her she is as unfailing as the Lord.
By his wisdom God founded the world, and by understanding he prepared the heavens.
By knowledge the depths were broken open, and the clouds poured down dew.
Son, do not slip away [?]; keep my counsels and commandments,
so that your soul may be saved and grace may be upon your head;
and may there be healing for your flesh and care for your bones,
so that you may walk in hope and peace in all your ways, and your foot will not stumble.
If you sit, you will sit without fear, and if you sleep, you will sleep in rest.
And you will not be afraid of terror that comes, nor of the attack of the ungodly when it arrives,
for the Lord will be in all your ways and will make your feet firm, so that you will not be shaken.
Do not hold back from doing good to the needy when your hand has the means to help.
Do not say, "Go away now, and tomorrow I will give to you; come back," if you have the power to do good.
Do not plot evil against your friend, who lives near you and trusts in you.
And do not become hostile [?; literally "enemy-loving"] toward a worthless man, or some evil may happen to you.
Do not take on the reproach of evil men, and do not imitate their ways,
for every lawless person is unclean before the Lord, and he does not dwell with the righteous.
The curse of the Lord is [?] in the houses of the ungodly, but the dwellings of the righteous are blessed by the Lord.
The Lord crushes the proud, but gives grace to the humble.
The wise will inherit glory, but the ungodly have exalted disgrace.
Children, listen to a father's instruction, and pay attention so that you may know understanding,
for I give you a good gift; do not forsake my law.
For I too was a son, obedient to my father and beloved in my mother's sight,
and they taught me and said to me: "Let my word be settled in your heart;
keep the commandments and do not forget them, and do not neglect the words of my mouth.
Do not turn away from the sayings of my mouth, and do not forsake it, and it will help you; love it, and it will guard you.
As the beginning of wisdom, acquire wisdom, and in exchange for all treasures, acquire understanding.
Put a wall around it, and it will lift you up; honor it, so that it may hold you dear,
so that it may place a crown of grace on your head and shield you with a crown of delight."
Listen, children, and accept my words, and the years of your life will be multiplied, so that many ways of life may be yours.
For I have taught you the ways of wisdom and the paths of the righteous.
If you walk, your steps will not be hindered, and if you run, you will not grow weary.
Hold fast to my teaching and do not abandon it, but keep it for yourself, for it is your life.
Do not go in the way of the ungodly, and do not imitate the ways of the lawless.
Do not go to the place where they set up camp. Turn your feet away from it and leave it behind,
for they do not sleep until they have done evil. Their strength has been taken from them, and they do not sleep,
they who are fed on the food of ungodliness and get drunk on the wine of lawlessness.
But the ways of the righteous shine like light. They go ahead and give light until the day is fully come.
But the ways of the ungodly are dark. They do not know where their foot will stumble.
My son, pay attention to my sayings and give your mind to my words,
so that your springs may not run dry for you. Keep them in your heart.
For they are life to those who find them, and relief to all flesh.
Let your heart keep every [?], for from these come the outgoings of life.
Remove a deceitful mouth from yourself, and put lying lips far away from you.
Let your eyes look straight ahead, and let your eyelids bear witness to righteousness.
Make straight the paths of your feet, and set your ways in the right direction.
Do not turn aside, either to the right or to the left. Turn your feet away from the evil way.
For the Lord knows the ways on the right, but the ways on the left are crooked.
He will make your paths straight and will lead your steps forward in peace.
My son, stay close to my wisdom and give your mind to my words,
so that you may keep good understanding. I am giving you the knowledge of my lips as a command.
Do not look at a wicked woman. Honey drips from the lips of a harlot. For a moment it sweetens your palate,
but afterward you will find it more bitter than gall and sharper than a two-edged sword.
For the feet of folly lead down those who have dealings with her. After death they fall down into hell, and her tracks are not steady.
For she does not come to the way of life; her paths are wandering and cannot be known.
Now, my son, listen to me, and do not disregard my words.
Keep your ways far from her, and do not go near the doors of her house,
so that you do not give your life to strangers and your possessions to the merciless,
so that strangers are not filled with your strength and your labours do not go into the house of others,
and you repent at the last, when the flesh of your body [lit. of your bones] is wasted away.
And you will say: "Why did I hate instruction, and why did my heart turn away from reproof?
I did not listen to the voice of my teacher, nor did I incline my ear to my instructor.
A little more, and I would have been found in every evil, in the midst of the gathering and the congregation."
Drink water from your own vessels and from your own wells.
Let water spring up for you from your own springs, and let your waters flow in your own streets.
Let them be your possession alone, and let no stranger share them with you.
Let that spring of water be your very own, and rejoice together with your youth.

Let the hart of love and the fawn of graces keep company with you; let that love be counted as yours and be with you at all times, for while you live with her in her love you will be greatly increased.
Do not linger with a strange woman, and do not embrace the arms of one who is not yours,
for a man's ways are before the eyes of God, and he sees all his paths.
Lawlessness ensnares a man, and each one is bound by the cord of his own sins.
Such a one dies among the uninstructed, through his own lack of instruction; he is cast out from the abundance of his wealth, and he perished through his own folly.
My son, if you have stood surety for your friend, you have given your hand to your enemy,
for a man's own lips are a strong snare, and he is caught by the lips of his own mouth.
My son, do what I command you, and be saved, for you have fallen into the hands of evil because of your friend. Be watchful and do not slacken; rouse also your friend, for whom you stood surety.
Give no sleep to your eyes, and do not let your eyelids slumber,
so that you may escape like a gazelle from the snare and like a bird from the trap.
Become like the ant, O sluggard: imitate its ways and become wiser than it.
For it has no land, and it has no overseer, and it is under no master.
which prepares its food in summer and gathers an abundant store on the threshing floors;
or go to the bee and learn how it works, and how well it does its labour,
whose labour kings and the poor take for their life. It is desired and honoured by all,
and though it is weak in strength, it honoured wisdom and was raised up.
How long will you lie there, O sluggard? When will you wake from sleep?
A little you sit, a little you doze, a little more, and you fold your hands upon your breast.
Then poverty will come upon you like an evil traveller, and want like a good runner.
If you are diligent, your harvest will come like a spring, and want will flee from you like an evil man.
A senseless and lawless man walks in a crooked way,
and such a one winks with his eye, signals with his foot, and makes signs by beckoning with his fingers.
With a perverse heart he does evil at all times; such a one stirs up trouble in the city.
Therefore his ruin comes upon him suddenly: being cut off, and a crushing that cannot be healed.
For he rejoices in everything that God hates, and he is crushed by the impurity of his own soul.
Insulting eyes and a lying tongue, hands that shed the blood of the righteous,
and a heart that devises evil thoughts, and feet that train themselves to do evil, will be destroyed.
And a false witness kindles lies and sends judgment among brothers.
My son, keep the laws of your father, and do not cast away the rules of your mother.
Set them upon your head always, and bind them around your neck.
When you walk, take them along and let them be with you; and when you sleep, let them guard you, so that when you rise they may talk with you;
for the commandment of the law is a light, and reproof and instruction are a light on the ways of life,
to keep you from another man's wife and from the scheming of a foreign tongue.
My son, do not let the beauty of desire overcome you; do not be caught by her eyes, and do not be led astray by her eyelids,
for the price of a prostitute is like that of a single loaf of bread, but a woman ensnares the precious souls of men.
Will anyone [?] bind fire in his bosom and his clothing not be burned?
Or does anyone walk on coals of fire and his feet not be burned?
So too, whoever goes in to a married woman will not escape torment, and likewise whoever touches her will not be innocent.
It is no wonder if someone is caught stealing; he steals to satisfy his hungry soul.
If he is caught, he will pay back sevenfold and give up all his goods, and so redeem himself.
But the adulterer, through lack of understanding, brings destruction on himself.
He endures pain and dishonour, and his disgrace will not be wiped away.
For her husband is full of jealousy and anger; he will not spare him in the day of judgement.
No amount of ransom will free him from his enmity, and he will not be appeased by many gifts.
My son, keep my words and hide my commandments within you.
My son, honour the Lord and you will be strong, and apart from him fear no one else.
Keep my commandments and you will live, and guard my words like the pupil of your eye.
Bind them on your fingers and write them on the breadth of your heart.
Call wisdom your sister, and make understanding your friend,
so that she may guard you from the strange and evil woman, if she speaks to you with deceitful words.
For she looks down into the streets from the window of her house,
and sees a young man, one of the foolish, lacking in understanding,
passing by the wall at the way out of her house,
and he talks in the darkness at evening, when the night is quiet and dark.
And the woman met him, dressed like a harlot, the kind that makes a young man's heart flutter.
She is wild and impure. Her feet cannot stay at home.
Sometimes she wanders [?] outside, sometimes in the streets; she watches at every corner.
Then she met him and kissed him with a shameless face and said to him:
"I have a peace offering; today I have fulfilled my vows.
That is why I came out to meet you. I longed to see your face, and I have found you.
I have fastened my bed with cords [?]; I have spread it with coverings from Egypt.
I have sprinkled my bed with saffron and my house with cinnamon."
Come, let us enjoy love until dawn; come, let us tumble together in passion,
for my husband is not at home in the house; he has gone on a long journey.
He took a bundle of silver in his hand; he will come back to his house after many days."
She led him astray with much persuasive talk, and with the snares of her lips she turned him aside.
And he followed her, beguiled, like an ox led to the stall, and like a dog to be tied up,
or like a deer whose liver an arrow has struck as it hurries on, and like a bird to the snare. He does not know that he is running toward evil for his own soul and seeking it.
Now, my son, listen to me and pay attention to the words of my mouth.
Do not let your heart turn aside to her ways,
for she has wounded and overthrown many, and those she has destroyed are beyond counting.
Her dwelling is the road to hell, and it leads down to the chambers of death.
Now therefore, proclaim wisdom, so that understanding may obey you,
for she stands on the high summits and is found among the places.
She has taken her stand at the gates of the mighty, and is praised at the entrances of the roads.
"I appeal to you, O children, and I raise my voice to the sons of men.
You who are innocent, understand knowledge, and you who are untaught, take it to heart.
Listen to me, for I speak good things to you, and I will open my lips to speak what is right.
For my mouth will practice truth; lying lips are hateful to me.
All the words of my mouth are spoken in righteousness, and there is nothing in them twisted or crooked.
They are all plain to those who understand them, and right to those who have found knowledge.
Take instruction rather than silver, and knowledge rather than choice gold.
Wisdom is better than precious jewels; no precious thing is equal to her worth.
I, Wisdom, have taken possession of the knowledge of counsel and of understanding, and I have called upon discernment.
The fear of the Lord hates wickedness, insolence and arrogance, the way of the wicked and crooked paths. And I have come to hate the mouth of the unbeliever.
Counsel is mine, vengeance is mine, strength is mine.
By me kings reign, and the mighty write down righteousness.
Through me the great are made great, and through me the mighty hold the earth.
I love those who love me, and those who seek me will find me.
Wealth and glory are mine, and many possessions, and righteousness.
To acquire me is better than gold and precious carbuncle, and my words are better than gold and choice silver.
I walk in the ways of righteousness and I go about among the places of justice,
so that I may share out fruit to those who love me and fill their treasuries with good things.
If I tell you day by day the things that happen, I will remember to recount the things from eternity.
The Lord established me as the beginning of his ways, for his works.
Before the ages he established me, in the beginning,
before the making of the earth and before the depths came to be, before the coming forth of the waters.
Before the mountains were founded, before all the hills, he begot me.
The Lord made the world, and the uninhabited lands, and the ends of the world that are under heaven.
When he was preparing the heavens, I was with him, and when he was setting his thrones upon the winds,
and when he was making the clouds above strong, and when he was carefully setting the springs under heaven,
when he set its law for the sea, so that the waters should not pass over its face, and when he was making firm the foundations of the earth,
I was before him. I was the one in whom the Lord rejoiced. Day by day I rejoiced before him, in his presence, at all times.
He rejoiced when he had completed the world as his creation; he rejoiced over the sons of men.
Now, my son, listen to me: blessed is the man who keeps my ways and keeps watch
at my doors, guarding the entrances of my thresholds day by day,
for my ways out are the ways out of life, and favour is prepared by the Lord.
But those who sin against me act wickedly against their own souls, and those who hate me love death.
Wisdom built a house for herself and set up seven pillars beneath it.
And she slaughtered her own sacrificial animals, mixed her wine in bowls, and prepared her table.
And she sent out her servants, proclaiming with a loud voice over the bowls, and she said:
"Whoever is foolish, let him turn aside to me." And to those lacking in understanding she said:
Come, eat my bread and drink the wine that I have mixed for you.
Leave folly behind, so that you may live and be alive, and set understanding straight with knowledge.
Whoever teaches the wicked brings disgrace on himself, and whoever reproves the ungodly defiles himself.
Do not reprove the ungodly, so that he does not hate you. Reprove a wise man and he will love you; reprove a fool and he will increase his hatred toward you.
Give a wise man an occasion and he will become wiser. Instruct a righteous man and he will grow in receiving instruction.
The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord,
and knowledge of the law comes from a good mind.
For in this way you will live a long time, and years of life will be added to you.
My son, if you are wise, you will be wise for yourself and for your neighbor as well. If you are wicked, you alone will be filled with evil, to your own harm.
Whoever relies on lies is like someone who herds the winds, and he watches the birds.
For he has abandoned the paths of his own vineyard and strayed from the tracks of the work of his own land.
He walks through a waterless desert and a land set apart and thirsty, and with his own hand he gathers barrenness.
A foolish and reckless woman, who knows no shame, will lack bread.
For she sat at the doors of her house, on seats, openly in the streets,
and she calls out to those passing by, who are keeping straight on their way:
"Whoever among you is senseless and lacking in understanding, I command him and say to him:
Eat hidden bread to your fill, and drink sweet hidden water."
But he does not know that the children of the earth perish because of her and are drawn down to the depths of hell.
Instead, flee and do not linger in that place, and do not fix your eyes on her.
So you will pass by a strange stream and cross over another river.
Keep away from strange water, and do not drink from another man's spring,
so that you may live a long time and the years of your life may be added to you.
A wise son makes his father glad, but a foolish son is his mother's grief.
The treasures of the lawless are of no profit, but righteousness will deliver from death.
The Lord will not let a righteous soul die of hunger, but he will overthrow the life of the ungodly.
Poverty humbles a man, but the hands of the strong make rich.
A son who is instructed will be wise, but the foolish one will serve like a slave.
A prudent son was saved from the heat, but a lawless son will be blasted by the wind on the threshing floors.
The blessing of the Lord is on the head of the righteous, but untimely mourning will cover the mouth of the ungodly.
The memory of the righteous will be with praise, but the house of the ungodly will be overthrown.
A wise man receives the commandments with his heart, but the one who cannot restrain his lips will be tripped up and made to stumble.
Whoever walks in uprightness walks in hope, but whoever twists his ways will be found out.
Whoever winks with the eye gathers sorrow for people; but whoever rebukes openly makes peace.
A fountain of life is in the soul of the righteous, but destruction will cover the mouth of the ungodly.
Hatred stirs up strife, and love covers all who are not quarrelsome.
Whoever brings forth wisdom from his lips strikes the foolish man with a rod.
The wise conceal knowledge,
but the ruin of the weak is poverty.
The work of the righteous produces life, but the fruit of the ungodly is sin.
Wisdom guards the ways of these times, but God guards the ways of life, and instruction that is not corrected goes astray.
The lips of the righteous conceal enmity, but those who bring forth abuse are fools.
With many words you will not escape sin; when you restrain your lips, you will be prudent.
The tongue of the righteous is refined silver, but the heart of the ungodly will fail.
The lips of the righteous know righteousness, but fools die in want.
Blessing is on the head of the righteous, and it will make him righteous, and sorrow will not be added to his heart.
A fool does evil with laughter, but wisdom gives birth to prudence in a man.
The ungodly man is swept away in destruction, but the desire of the righteous is accepted.
When the storm passes by, the ungodly are destroyed, but the righteous man turns aside and is saved forever.
As unripe grapes are harmful to the teeth and smoke to the eyes, so is lawlessness to those who practise it.
The fear of the Lord adds to one's days, but the years of the ungodly will be shortened.
Joy remains with the righteous, but the hope of the ungodly will perish.
The fear of the Lord is a stronghold for the righteous, but ruin comes upon those who do evil.
The righteous will never sin, but the ungodly will not dwell in the land.
Wisdom comes out of the mouth of the righteous, but the lying tongue will be destroyed.
Grace comes from the lips of righteous men, but the mouth of the ungodly will be overthrown.
Deceitful balances are an abomination before the Lord, but a just scale pleases him.
Wherever insolence enters, dishonor is there too, but a humble mouth trains itself in wisdom.
When the righteous man died he left behind regret, but the destruction of the ungodly is swift and brings relief.
The righteousness of the blameless keeps his ways straight, but ungodliness falls upon the false.
The righteousness of righteous men delivers them, but the lawless are destroyed by their folly.
At the end of a righteous man, hope does not fail, but the boasting of the ungodly will be destroyed.
The righteous is rescued from the wild beast, and the ungodly is handed over in his place.
A snare for the citizens is in the mouth of the lawless,
but the understanding of the righteous governs the city.
A city is raised up by the blessing of the upright, but it is torn down by the mouth of the ungodly.
A person who lacks sense treats his fellow citizens with contempt, but a sensible man lives quietly.
A double-tongued man reveals plans in the assembly, but one who is faithful in spirit keeps matters hidden.
Those who have no guidance fall like leaves, but life is found in much counsel.
A wicked man does evil when he mingles with the righteous, and he hates the [?] of caution.
A gracious woman raises up glory, but a woman who hates justice is a seat of dishonor. The lazy come to lack wealth, but the strong are made secure by wealth.
A merciful man does good to his own soul, but a merciless man destroys his own flesh.
The ungodly does the work of falsehood, but the seed of the righteous is the reward of truth.
A righteous son is born for life, but the pursuit of the ungodly leads to death.
Perverse ways are an abomination to the Lord, but all the blameless are acceptable to him.
Whoever joins hands with falsehood will not go unpunished, but whoever sows righteousness will receive a sure reward,
Beauty in an evil-natured woman is like a ring in a pig's snout.
Everything the righteous desire is good, but the hope of the ungodly will perish.
There are those who sow what is their own and gather more, and there are those who gather what belongs to others and end up in want.
Every blessed soul is sincere, but a hot-tempered man is not seemly.
Whoever hoards grain, may it be left to the nations. Those who [?] grain grudgingly are cursed by the people, but blessing rests on the head of the generous.
Whoever does good seeks the favor that comes from good, but whoever searches out evil will be overtaken by it.
Whoever trusts in riches will fall, but those who help the righteous will shine forth.
Whoever does not live in harmony with his own household will inherit the winds, and the fool will serve the wise.
From the fruit of righteousness the tree of life springs up, but the souls of the lawless are taken away before their time.
If the righteous is barely saved, where then will the sinner and the ungodly appear?
Whoever loves instruction loves wisdom, but whoever hates reproof is a fool.
Better is the one who has found wisdom from the Lord, but the lawless man will be put to silence.
A man will not prosper through lawlessness, and the roots of the ungodly will be torn up.
A sensible woman is her husband's crown. As a worm destroys wood, so an evil-doing woman destroys her husband.
The thoughts of the righteous are better, but the ungodly steer by deceit.
The words of the lawless plot treacherously to shed blood, but the mouth of the righteous will rescue them;
wherever the ungodly turns, he will be destroyed, but the houses of the righteous will stand firm.
A man praises the mouth of the prudent, but the one who is sick at heart will be held in contempt.
A man who lives humbly and serves himself is better off than one who seeks honor and lacks bread.
The righteous man has compassion on the lives of his livestock, but the heart of the ungodly is merciless.
Whoever works his own land will have plenty of bread, but those who chase after vanity are senseless.
Those whose conduct will leave a reproach in their own dwellings, [?]
The desires of the ungodly are evil, but the roots of the godly are in strongholds.
Through the sin of his lips the sinner falls into a snare, but the righteous escapes from it.
Whoever looks with sincerity will find mercy, but whoever confronts people at the gates oppresses them.
A man's soul will be filled with good things from the fruit of his mouth, and the reward of his lips will be given to him.
The ways of fools seem right in their own eyes, but a wise man listens to counsel.
The fool shows his anger day after day, but a prudent man hides his disgrace.
The righteous man declares open faithfulness, but the witness of liars is deceitful.
There are some whose words cut like a sword, but the tongue of the wise brings healing.
Truthful lips make testimony stand firm, but a hasty witness has a lying tongue.
Deceit is in the heart of the one who does evil, but those who want to make peace will rejoice.
Nothing false pleases the righteous man, but the ungodly will be filled with evil.
Deceitful lips are an abomination to the Lord, but whoever acts faithfully is acceptable to him.
A man of understanding is a throne of knowledge, but the heart of fools will meet with a curse.
The hand of the chosen will easily take hold, but the deceitful will be taken captive.
A terrible word makes the heart of a righteous man tremble, but good news makes him glad.
The righteous man is understanding toward his own friend; but evil will overtake the one who sins, and the ways of the ungodly will lead him astray.
The deceitful man will not catch any game, but a pure man is a precious possession.
In the ways of righteousness there is life, but the ways of those who bear grudges lead to death.
A sensible son obeys his father, but a disobedient son will be handed over to destruction.
The prudent man will eat of the fruit of righteousness, but the souls of the ungodly will perish before their time.
Whoever guards his mouth keeps his soul safe, but the rash man will bring terror on himself.
Every idle man is caught up in his desires, but the hands of the strong are busy at hard work.
The righteous man hates a slanderous word, but the ungodly man is put to shame and will have no confidence.
Righteousness guards the innocent, but sin brings the ungodly to nothing.
There are some who make themselves out to be rich and have nothing, and there are some who humble themselves in the midst of great wealth.
A man's own wealth is the ransom of his soul, but a poor man cannot stand up to threats.
The light of the righteous lasts forever, but the light of the ungodly will be put out.
Deceitful hearts go astray in sin, but the righteous have pity and show mercy.
The wicked man does evil with insolence, but those who know their own minds are wise.
Wealth gathered in haste through lawlessness will dwindle, but whoever gathers for himself through godliness will see it grow.
Better is the one who starts to help with his heart than the one who only promises. The righteous man shows mercy and lends, for a good desire belongs to life.
Whoever despises a matter will be ruined by it, but those who fear these commandments live.
Nothing good will come to a deceitful son, but a wise servant's affairs will prosper and his way will succeed.
The law of the wise is a fountain of life, but the fool will be caught in a snare and die.
Good understanding brings favor, and knowing the law belongs to a good mind, but the ways of the scornful lead to destruction.
Every wise man acts with knowledge, but the fool shows his own wickedness.
A hot-tempered king will fall into evil, but a faithful witness will deliver him.
Instruction takes away poverty and dishonor, but whoever heeds reproof will be glorified.
The desires of the godly make the soul glad, but the deeds of the ungodly are far from knowledge.
If you walk with the wise, you will be wise; but whoever keeps company with fools will be known for it.
Evil will overtake those who sin, but good will come to the righteous.
A good man will leave an inheritance to his grandchildren, and the wealth of the ungodly is stored up for the righteous.
The righteous will spend many years in wealth, but liars will quickly perish.
Whoever spares the rod from his son hates him, but whoever loves him disciplines him diligently.
The righteous man eats and satisfies his soul, but the souls of the ungodly go hungry.
Wise women build up houses, but the one who is foolish tears hers down with her own hand.
Whoever walks uprightly fears the Lord, but whoever makes his ways crooked will be dishonored.
From the mouth of fools comes a rod of insult, but the lips of the righteous protect them.
Where there are no oxen, the mangers are clean; but where the harvest is great, the strength of the ox is plain to see.
A faithful witness does not lie, but a false witness stirs up lies.
If you look for wisdom among the wicked, you will not find it; knowledge comes easily to the prudent.
Everything stands against a foolish man, but the lips of the wise are weapons of knowledge.
The wisdom of those who have knowledge shows in their ways, but the folly of fools leads them astray.
The houses of the lawless are bound for destruction, but the houses of the righteous are accepted.
The soul of a discerning heart is sorrowful, and when it rejoices, it does not join in insult.
The houses of the ungodly will be destroyed, but the houses of the righteous will be established.
There are ways that people think are right, but their end reaches the depths of hell.
Sorrow does not mix with joy, but in the end joy turns to mourning.
The hard-hearted man will have his fill of his own ways, and the good man of his own counsels.
The innocent person believes every word, but the prudent person turns to repentance.
The wise man was afraid and turned away from evil, but the fool joined in confidently.
The hot-tempered man acts without thinking, but the prudent man is very patient.
The foolish will share evil among themselves, but the wise will take hold of the gates of the righteous.
The wicked will stumble before the good, and the ungodly will serve at the gates of the righteous.
Friends hate a poor friend, but the rich have many friends.
Whoever despises the poor sins, but whoever has mercy on the poor will be blessed.
Those who go astray do evil, but the good do mercy and truth. Those who do evil do not know mercy and faithfulness, but mercy and faithfulness belong to those who do good.
In all careful effort there is abundance, but the pleasure-seeker and the pitiless will be in want.
Wealth is the crown of the wise, but the conduct of fools is evil.
A faithful witness rescues a soul from evil, but a deceitful one stirs up lies.
In the fear of the Lord there is strong hope, and he leaves zeal for righteousness to his children.
The command of the Lord is a fountain of life, and it brings deliverance from the snare of death.
A king's glory lies in a multitude of nations, but a ruler's ruin lies in a dwindling people.
A patient man is great in understanding, but a short-tempered man is extremely foolish.
A gentle man is a healer of the heart, and a heart of knowledge is healing for the bones.
Whoever slanders the poor angers his Maker, but whoever honors the Lord has mercy on the poor.
The ungodly man is driven away by his own wickedness, but whoever trusts in his own holiness is righteous.
Wisdom enters the heart of a good man, but in the heart of fools it cannot be found.
Righteousness exalts nations, but souls are diminished through sin.
An intelligent servant is pleasing to the king; by his own good conduct he removes dishonor.
Anger destroys even the wise. If an answer falls in between, it turns away wrath. A grievous word stirs up anger,
but the tongue of the wise knows what is good, while the mouth of fools tells evil.
In every place the eyes of the Lord watch the good and the evil.
The healing of the tongue is a tree of life, and whoever keeps it will be filled with spirit.
A fool despises his father's instruction, but whoever heeds reproof will be wiser.

In the justifying of righteousness there is great strength, but the ungodly will perish utterly, root and all, from the earth. In the house of the righteous there is much strength, but the fruits of the ungodly will perish.
The lips of the wise are clothed with knowledge, but the heart of fools is not careful.
The sacrifices of the ungodly are an abomination to the Lord, but the prayers of the righteous are acceptable to the Lord.
The ways of the ungodly are an abomination before him, but he loves those who look to righteousness.
The instruction of the innocent is recognized by those who pass by, but those who hate reproof come to a shameful end.
Hell and destruction lie open before the Lord; how much more the hearts of men.
The uninstructed person will not love his teachers, and he does not take counsel with the wise.
When the heart is glad, the face too is cheerful, but those who are in sorrow have a sorrowful face.
An upright heart seeks knowledge, but the mouth of the uninstructed will know evil.
At all times the eyes of the wicked look for evil, but the good are always at rest.
Better a small portion with the fear of the Lord than great treasures without fear.
Better a meal of herbs with love and kindness than calves slaughtered from the stalls with enmity.
A hot-tempered man prepares strife, but [?]
A patient man quenches judgment, but the ungodly man stirs it up all the more.
The ways of the idle are strewn with thorns, but those of the diligent are smooth [?].
A wise son makes his father glad, but a disobedient child despises his mother.
The ignorant person becomes lacking in heart, but a man of understanding walks uprightly.
Those who do not honor the council put off [?] their plans, but counsel abides in the hearts of the shrewd.
Let not the wicked man quarrel with him, nor say anything complete and fine at all.
The way of life is the intent of the wise, so that he may turn away from hell and be saved.
The Lord pulls down the houses of the insolent, but he establishes the boundaries of the orphan and the widow.
Lying thoughts are hateful to the Lord, for the words of the Lord are holy and worthy.
He who takes a bribe destroys himself, but he who hates bribes will be saved.
Sins are cleansed by almsgiving and by faith, and by the fear of God everyone turns away from evil.
And let the hearts of the righteous be trained in faith, but the mouth of the ungodly answers with evil.
The ways of righteous men are accepted by the Lord, and through them even enemies become friends.
The Lord keeps far away from the ungodly, but he hears the prayer of the righteous.
A small income with righteousness is better than abundant fruit with falsehood.
Let a man's heart plan righteousness, so that his steps may be guided by God.
When the eye sees what is good, it gladdens the heart, and good news fattens the bones.
He who listens to the reproof of life will rest among the wise.
He who pushes instruction away from himself hates himself, but he who keeps reproof will gain wisdom.
The fear of the Lord is instruction and wisdom, and he will gain the leadership of glory.
Directing the heart is up to man, but the gain [?] of the tongue comes from the Lord. The greater you are, the more you should humble yourself, and you will find favour before the Lord God.
All the works of the humble are plain to see before the Lord, but the ungodly will be destroyed on the evil day.
Roll your works onto the Lord and turn them toward him, so that your thoughts may be made firm.
The Lord made everything for his own sake, but the ungodly will perish on the evil day.
Everyone who is proud of heart is unclean before the Lord, and whoever joins hands in falsehood will be guilty.
The beginning of a good way is doing what is right; that is more pleasing before the Lord than offering sacrifices.
But whoever seeks God will find knowledge together with righteousness, and whoever seeks him rightly will find peace.
For all the works of God are done in righteousness, but the ungodly man is kept for the evil day.
Divination is on the lips of the king, and his mouth will not go wrong in judgement.
The weight of the scale of righteousness comes from the Lord, for his works are a scale of righteousness.
Doing evil is abominable to the king, for the throne of rule is established by righteousness.
Righteous lips are pleasing to the king, and he loves righteous words.
The king's wrath is an angel of death, but a wise man will appease him.
The king's son is in the light of life, and those who are pleasing to him are like a cloud of late rain.
Nests of wisdom are better than gold, and nests of understanding are more precious than silver.

The paths of life turn aside from evil, and the ways of righteousness are length of days. Whoever receives instruction will be among good things, and whoever heeds reproof will become wise. Whoever keeps the ways of the Lord will guard his soul, and whoever loves his life will be careful with his mouth.
Insolence goes before destruction, and an evil [?] disposition before a fall.
Better is one who is gentle in mind and humble than one who divides the spoil with the insolent.
One who is understanding in matters will find good things, but one who trusts in the Lord will be blessed.
The wise and prudent are called understanding, but those who are sweet in words will be heard more.
Understanding is a fountain of life to those who have gained it, but the instruction of fools is evil.
The heart of the wise man understands from his own mouth, and he wears knowledge on his lips.
Good words are a honeycomb, and their sweetness is healing for the soul.
There are ways that seem right to people, but their end looks into the depths of hell.
A man in pain toils for himself and forces off his own destruction, but the perverse man carries destruction in his own mouth.
A foolish man digs up evil for himself and stores up fire on his lips.
A perverse man sends out evil, sets the spark of deceit like fire to the wicked, and separates friends.
A lawless man puts his friends to the test and leads them on a way that is not good.
Whoever fixes his eyes plots perversity, and brings all this evil near with his lips, for he is a furnace of wickedness.
Wisdom is a crown of glory, and it is found in the ways of righteousness.
A patient man is better than a strong one, and whoever restrains his anger is greater than one who captured a strong city.
Everything comes back into the bosom of liars, but from the Lord everything is just.
A little bread eaten with relish and in peace is better than a house full of every good thing, with sacrifices of falsehood and with strife.
A wise servant will rule over foolish masters and will receive his share among brothers.
As silver and gold are tested in the furnace, so God tests hearts.
The wicked man listens to the tongue of the lawless, but the righteous man pays no attention to lying lips.
He who mocks the poor angers his Maker, and he who rejoices over one who is perishing will not go unpunished.
Grandchildren are the crown of the old, and fathers are the pride of their children.
Trustworthy lips do not suit fools, nor do lying lips suit the righteous.
Instruction is a reward of grace to those who use it; wherever it turns, it will prosper him.
He who conceals a falsehood seeks love, but he who hates to keep it hidden separates friends and members of the household.
A word crushes the heart of a prudent man, but a fool, even when he is punished, does not perceive it.
Every wicked man stirs up contention, but the Lord will send a merciless angel against him.
Worry falls upon a man of understanding, but a fool plots evil.
Whoever repays evil for good, evil will not depart from his house.
Authority is given to the beginnings of righteousness, but strife and quarreling lead the way to want.
Whoever justifies the false and makes the righteous out to be false, both of these are abominable before the Lord.
Why has wealth been given to a fool? For the fool is not able to acquire wisdom.
He who raises his own house high is seeking its ruin, and he who is perverse about learning will be bound up in evil.
Have a friend at all times, but brothers are useful in trouble, for this is why they are born.
A foolish man claps his hands and rejoices over himself, the one who becomes surety for his own friends.
The lover of sin delights in strife,
and the hard-hearted man will not attain good; a man who twists his words with his tongue will suddenly fall into evil.
The heart of fools is a grief to the one who begot them. A father does not rejoice over an uninstructed son,
but a cheerful heart brings about what is good and bright, while the bones of a sorrowful man dry up.
He who takes a bribe into his bosom deceitfully, his ways will not prosper; the ungodly man turns aside from the way of righteousness.
The face of a man of understanding is wise, but the eyes of a fool are on the ends of the earth.
A foolish son is a cause of anger to his father and a grief to the one who bore him.
It is not good to punish a righteous man, nor to plot evil against righteous rulers.
He who takes care not to speak a harsh word is prudent, and a patient man is wise.
When a fool has asked about something, it is counted to him as wisdom. He made himself silent, like one gathered in understanding, and it was thought that he is wise.
A man who wishes to separate from his friends looks for a pretext, but he will be open to blame at all times.
One who lacks understanding has no need of wisdom; rather, he takes up folly.
When the ungodly man reaches the depth of wickedness, then he shows contempt, but dishonor and reproach come upon him.
The word in a man's heart is deep water; a river springs from it, and a fountain of life.
It is not good to show favor to an ungodly man, nor is it right to pervert justice in judgment.
A fool's lips lead him into evil, and his rash mouth calls for death.
A fool's mouth is his own ruin, and his lips are a snare for his own soul.
Fear casts down the lazy man, and the souls of those who go after other men's wives will go hungry.
Whoever heals him by his own deeds is the brother of the one who destroys him.
The name of God comes from great strength; the righteous run to it and are lifted up.
A rich man's wealth is like a walled city, and his glory gives him great cover.
Before his downfall a man's heart is lifted up, and before glory it is humbled.
Whoever answers a word before he has heard it shows his folly and earns reproach.
A sensible servant calms a man's anger, but who will put up with a faint-hearted man?
The sensible heart gains knowledge, and the ears of the wise seek understanding.
A man's gift makes room for him and seats him among the mighty.
The righteous man accuses himself at his very first word, but as soon as his opponent brings his case, he is refuted.
The silent man puts an end to disputes, and he settles them among the mighty.
A brother helped by his brother is like a strong and high city, and he is as strong as a walled royal stronghold.
A man fills his belly from the fruit of his mouth, and he is satisfied from the fruit of his lips.
Death and life are in the power of the tongue, and those who guard it will eat its fruit.
Whoever has found a good wife has found grace and has received gladness from God.
Whoever drives out a good wife has driven out what is good, and whoever keeps an adulteress is foolish and ungodly.
The poor man asks with pleading, but the rich man answers with idle chatter.
A man who is a friend to his friend will be loved more than a brother.
Better is an ignorant man who walks faithfully than one who [?] with the duplicity of his lips.
Ignorance of one's own soul is not good, and restless feet run into sins.
A man's folly corrupts his ways, and in his heart he blames God.
Wealth gains many friends, but even the one friend a poor man has turns away from him.
A false witness will not go unpunished, and whoever brings false accusations will not escape.
Many serve in the presence of kings, but every one of them turns wicked over his gift and becomes a reproacher of the man.

Everyone who hates a poor brother will be far even from love. Good counsel is a reprover to those who know it, and a wise man has found it. Whoever does much evil pays tribute to wickedness, and whoever [?provokes] with words will not be saved.
Whoever has gained understanding loves his own self, and whoever keeps wisdom will find good.
A lying witness will not go unpunished, and he stirs up evil among the citizens. Whoever has stirred up evil will perish.
Luxury does not suit a fool, and neither does it suit a slave to rule over his masters with insolence.
A merciful man is patient, and his glory overtakes the lawless.
A king's word is like the roar of a lion, and his good favour is like dew on the grass.
A foolish son is a shame to his father, and prayers paid for with the wages of a strange woman are not pure.
Fathers divide house and property among their sons, but a wife is joined to a husband by the Lord.
Fear seizes the heart of adulterers, and the soul of the idle goes hungry.
Whoever keeps the commandments guards his own soul, but whoever neglects his ways will perish.
Whoever has mercy on the poor lends to the Lord, and he will repay him according to what he has given.
Discipline your son, and so there will be good hope. Do not lift up your soul to insolence. If you strike him with a rod he will not die, but his soul will be delivered from death.
A man will be severely punished for his malice, and if he goes on acting lawlessly, he will forfeit his own soul as well.
My son, listen to your father's instruction, so that you may be wise in your latter days.
There are many thoughts in a man's heart, but the counsel of the Lord stands forever.
Mercy is the fruit of a man, and a righteous poor man is better than a rich man who lies.
The fear of the Lord brings a man life, but the one without fear goes astray and wanders at the gates, in places that knowledge does not look upon.
Whoever unjustly hides his hands in his bosom will not even bring them to his mouth.
When a lawless man is punished, the foolish man becomes shrewder. If you rebuke a man of understanding, he will understand knowledge.
A son who dishonors his father and drives away his mother will be put to shame and reproach.
A son who neglects to keep his father's instruction will learn evil words.
He who takes responsibility for a foolish servant insults justice, and the mouth of the ungodly will swallow up judgment.
Punishments are prepared for the impure, and blows likewise for the foolish.
It is an impure thing for people to use much wine, and drunkenness is shameful; and no one who gets mixed up with these can be wise.
The threat of a king is no less than the wrath of a lion, and whoever provokes him sins against his own soul.
It is to a man's glory to turn away from abuse, but every fool gets entangled in such things.
You reproach the sluggard and he is not ashamed; so too is the one who borrows wheat at the threshing floors.
The thought of a man's heart is deep water, but a man of understanding will draw it out.
Man is a great thing, and a merciful man is precious, but a faithful man is hard to find.
Whoever lives blamelessly in righteousness will leave blessedness to his children.
When a righteous king sits on the throne, no evil whatever will rise up to oppose him before his eyes.
Who can boast that he has a pure heart? Or who will dare to say, "I am pure from sins"?
Whoever speaks evil of his father and mother, his lamp will be put out.
A portion gained hastily at the beginning will not be blessed in the end.
Do not say, "I will pay back my enemies," but be patient, so that the Lord may help you.
A large and a small weight and a double measure: both of these are unclean before the Lord,
and in his deeds the young man will be bound together with the worthy, and his ways are upright.
The ear hears and the eye sees, and both of these are the Lord's work.
Do not love evil speaking, so that you are not uprooted; open your eyes and be filled with bread.
A double weight is abominable to the Lord, and a deceitful balance (literally "yoke") is not good.
A man's way is directed by the Lord; how then can a mortal understand his own ways?
It is a snare to a man to promise something of his own hastily, for after the promise comes regret.
A righteous king scatters the ungodly and lays the yoke upon them.
The light of the Lord is the spirit of human beings, which searches the treasuries of the heart.
Mercy and truth are the guardians of the king, and they surround his thrones with righteousness.
The adornment of young men is wisdom, and the glory of the old is grey hair.
Restraint [?] and crushing will come upon the wicked man, and wounds upon the treasuries of the belly.
Like a rush of water is the king's heart in the hand of God: wherever he directs it, there it turns.
Every man seems righteous to himself, but the Lord directs the heart.
Doing righteousness and truth pleases the Lord more than sacrifices of blood.
A proud mind is hard-hearted in insolence [?], and the great brightness of the ungodly is sin.
To take counsel briefly is sincerity, but everyone who is unsteady will become [?].
Whoever gathers treasures with a lying tongue, it is in vain, and he is pursuing the snares of death.
Destruction will come upon the ungodly, because they do not want to do what is just.
To the crooked God sends crooked ways, for his works are pure and right.
It is better to live in the corner of a fence under the open sky than in houses plastered with falsehood, in a defiled shared house.
The soul of the ungodly will not be pitied by anyone who sees him.
When the wicked man is punished, the innocent becomes wiser, and the wise man understands and receives knowledge.
And the righteous man understands the ways of the ungodly; the ungodly are ruined in evil.
Whoever stops his ears so as not to hear the weak, he too will call on the Lord, and he will not hear him.
A secret gift turns away wrath, but whoever is grudging with a gift stirs up strong anger.
The joy of the righteous is doing righteousness, but this is unholy in the eyes of evildoers.
A man who has strayed from the ways of righteousness will rest in the assembly of the giants.
A needy man loves the enjoyment of friends, and wine and oil as wealth.
The lawless man is the refuse [?] of the righteous.
It is better to live in a desert land than with a babbling, talkative and angry woman.
A desirable treasure rests in the mouth of the wise, but foolish men swallow it up.
In the ways of righteousness and mercy they will find life.
A wise man came against strong cities and tore down the strongholds they trusted in.
Whoever guards his mouth and tongue keeps his soul from trouble.
A rash and arrogant man is called vile, and one who holds on to wrongs is called lawless.
Desires kill the lazy man, because his hands are unwilling to do any work.
The ungodly man craves evil things all day long, but the righteous man has compassion and shows mercy without holding back.
The sacrifices of the ungodly are hateful to the Lord, because they offer them lawlessly.
A lying witness will perish, but an obedient man speaks with care.
An ungodly man shamelessly stands up to others face to face, but the upright man understands his own ways.
There is no human wisdom, no human courage, and no plan that can stand against God.
A horse is made ready for the day of battle, but help comes from the Lord.
A good name is better than great wealth, and good favour is worth more than gold, silver and carbuncle.
The rich and the poor met one another, but the Lord made them both.
A shrewd man saw a wicked man being punished and said, “He will learn a hard lesson.” But fools passed by and paid the penalty.
Wisdom gives birth to the fear of the Lord, and to wealth, glory and life.
Thorns [?] and snares lie on crooked paths, but whoever guards himself will keep away from them.
The rich oppress the poor, and servants lend to their own masters.
Whoever sows wickedness will reap evil, and the blow brought on by his deeds will reach its full end.
Whoever has mercy on the poor will be fed in return, because he gave some of his own bread to the poor.
Whoever gives a bribe wins victory and honour, but the soul of the one who takes it will perish.
Drive the vile man out of the assembly, and victory will leave with him. When he sits in the assembly, he dishonours everyone.
The Lord loves those who are pure in heart, and all the blameless are acceptable to him. A wise king shepherds with his lips.
The eyes of the Lord guard knowledge, but the lawless man makes words empty.
The lazy man makes excuses and says, “There is a lion on the roads, and murderers in the streets.”
The mouth of the lawless is a deep pit, and whoever is hated by the Lord will fall into it.
There are evil ways before a man, and he does not like to turn away from them. But one must turn away from a crooked and evil way.
Folly is kindled in the heart of a youth, for the rod and instruction are far from him.
Whoever falsely accuses the poor man increases his own evil, and his wealth will be given to one in want.
Incline your ear to the word of the wise, and hear my words, and make your heart firm, so that you may know that they are good.
And if you gather them in your heart, they will gladden you, together, upon your lips,
so that your hope may be in the Lord, and he may make your way known to you.
And you, write them on your heart threefold, for counsel and for knowledge, in the breadth of your soul.
So I teach you a true word, and obedience to good knowledge, so that you may answer with the word of truth those who put a word to you.
Do not oppress the downtrodden because he is poor, and do not treat the downtrodden with contempt at the gates,
for the Lord will judge his cause, and you will deliver your soul in safety.
Do not become the friend of a hot-tempered man, and do not keep company with a wrathful companion,
lest you learn his ways and take a snare for your soul.
Do not give yourself as surety out of shame before someone's face.
If he has nothing to give, they will take your bed out from under your sides.
Do not alter the ancient boundaries that your fathers set.
A fine man who is quick in his work is worthy to stand before kings, and not to stand before sluggish men.
If you sit down to dine at the table of a powerful man, consider carefully what is set before you,
and only then put out your hand. Know that it is fitting for you to prepare such things.
If you are greedy, do not desire his foods, for these belong to a life of [?] all.
If you are poor, do not strain yourself to keep up with the rich man, and keep away from him in your understanding.
If you fix your eyes on it, it will not be seen, for wings like an eagle's are made ready for it, and it will return to the house of the one who reviles him [?].
Do not eat with an envious man, and do not desire his foods,
for he will eat and drink with you as someone who swallows a hair.
And do not bring him in and eat bread with him, for he will vomit it up and revile your good words.
Say nothing in the ears of a fool, lest he despise your wise words.
Do not move the ancient boundaries, and do not encroach on the property of orphans,
For their Redeemer is the Lord, the Mighty One, and he will judge their cause against you.
Give your heart to instruction, and make your ears ready for words of knowledge.
Do not withhold instruction from a young child; if you strike him with a rod, he will not die.
You will strike him with the rod, but you will save his soul from death.
My son, if your heart is wise, you will gladden my heart as well.
And if the words of your mouth [?] my lips,
do not imitate sinners in your heart, but remain in fear all your days.
If you keep these things, you will have offspring, and your hope will not be taken away from you.
Listen, my son, and become wise, and guide understanding in your heart.
Do not be a wine-drinker, and do not look to feasts shared with others or to the buying of meat,
for every drunkard and fornicator will become poor, and every drowsy person will be clothed in ragged clothing.
Listen, my son, to your father who begot you, and do not despise your mother because she has grown old.
A righteous father raises his children well, and his heart rejoices over a wise son.
Let your father and your mother rejoice over you, and gladden those who gave birth to you.
Give me your heart, my son, and let your eyes keep watch over my ways!
For another's house is a jar with a hole in it, and a stranger's pit is narrow.
For in an instant he will be stopped and will perish, and every lawless person will be destroyed.
Who has woe? Who has strife? Who has judgment and trouble? Who has sorrows? Who has bruises for no reason? Whose eyes are bleary?
Is it not those who linger over wine? Those who ask, "Where are the drinking bouts?"

Do not get drunk on wine, but talk with righteous people, and talk with one another as you walk. If you give your eyes to bowls and cups, in the end you will walk about more naked than the head of a pestle.
But in the end it will spread through him like a serpent's bite, and like a horned serpent's venom it will be [?] in him.
When your eyes see a strange woman, then your mouth will speak perverse things.
And you will sink down as into the heart of the sea, and like a ship's pilot amid many waves.
And then you will say: "They struck me and it did not hurt me, and they mocked me and I did not know it. When will dawn come, so that I may go out and look for those I went about with?"
My son, do not imitate evil people, and do not let your heart desire to be with them,
For his tongue is trained in falsehood, and their lips speak of trouble.
By wisdom a house is built, and by understanding it is set up.
By knowledge the treasuries are filled, full of all precious and good wealth.
A wise man is better than a strong one, and a man who has understanding is better than a great farm.
War is waged with guidance, but help comes from a heart that gives counsel.
Wisdom and good understanding are at the gates of the wise; the wise do not turn aside from the face of God,
but they deliberate in the assembly. Death will befall the untaught.
And the fool will die in sin, and through uncleanness a man will be defiled with filth
in the evil day and in the day of battle, without fail.
Rescue those who have been handed over to death. Do not spare,
if you say, "I did not know these things"; for the Lord knows the hearts of all. He who created souls knows everything, and he will repay each person according to their deeds.
Eat honey, my son, for the honeycomb is good, so that your palate may be sweetened.
In the same way you will come to know wisdom for your soul. If you find it, your end will be good, and hope will not forsake you.
Do not bring an ungodly man into the dwelling of the righteous, and do not be led astray by a full belly.
Even if the righteous man falls seven times, he will rise again, but the ungodly will grow weak in evil.
If your enemy falls, do not be glad about it; do not exalt yourself over his stumbling,
lest the Lord see it and be displeased, and turn his wrath away from him.
Do not rejoice over evildoers, and do not imitate sinners,
for the wicked man will have no offspring, and the brightness of the ungodly will be put out.
Fear God, my son, and the king, and do not be disobedient to either of them,
for the ungodly will suddenly cry out, and who can know the punishment that comes from these two?
The son who keeps the word will be rescued from destruction; he has been fully accepted,
and no lie will come out of his mouth.
The king's tongue is a sword, and not one of flesh; whoever among men is handed over to it will be destroyed, sinews and all.
It devours men's bones and burns them up like a flame, so that they are not fit to eat even for the young of eagles.
And this I say to you who are wise, so that you may understand: it is not good to show partiality in judgment.
Whoever says of the ungodly man, "He is righteous," shall be cursed by the people and hated by the nations.
But those who rebuke him will be seen as better, and a good blessing will come upon them.
Lips will kiss the answer of good words, but whoever is double-hearted in words sets out his words face to face [?].
Under the open sky prepare your works for going out, and make yourself ready for the field, and walk after me, and your house will be built.
Do not be a false witness against your fellow citizen, and do not speak too freely with your lips.
Do not say, "As he did to me, so I will do to him; I will pay him back as much as he harmed me."
A foolish man is like a farmed field, and a man who lacks understanding is like a vineyard.
If you leave it alone, it will become desolate and completely overgrown with grass. It will fail, and its stone walls will be broken down.
Afterward I repented, and I looked to choose instruction.
"A little while I slumber, a little while I sleep, and a little while I fold my hands on my chest."
If you do this, your poverty will come upon you like a forerunner, and your want like a good runner.
These are the miscellaneous instructions of Solomon, which the friends of Hezekiah, king of Judea, copied out.
The glory of God conceals words, but the glory of a king honours deeds.
Heaven is high and the earth is deep, but the heart of a king cannot be searched out.
Beat out untested silver, and it will be refined until it is completely pure.
Let the heathen be destroyed from before the king, and his throne will be set straight in righteousness.
Do not behave boastfully before the king, and do not stand in the place of the mighty.
It is better for you to be told, "Come up to me," than to be humbled before the mighty. Speak of what your eyes have seen:
Do not be quick to quarrel, so that you do not regret it in the end, when your friend reproaches you.
Turn away from him and do not despise him,
or your friend may reproach you, and your quarrel and enmity will not leave you but will be like death to you.
Grace and friendship set a person free. Keep them for yourself, so that you do not become someone open to reproach, but keep your ways well.
Like a golden ball on a sardius necklace is the speaking of a word.
A word of wisdom to obedient ears is adorned like a golden earring and a precious carbuncle.
As snow falling on a mountain in the heat is a benefit, so is a faithful messenger to those who send him; he is a benefit to the hearts of those who call for him.
Like winds and clouds and harsh rains are those who boast falsely of a gift.
Patience makes the ways of kings prosper, and a soft tongue breaks bones.
Have you found honey? Eat only as much as is fitting, or you may have too much and vomit it up.
Rarely set your foot in your friend's house, or he may grow tired of you and come to hate you.
Like a club, a sword and a sharp arrow is a man who bears false witness against his friend.
The way of the wicked and the foot of the lawless will perish on an evil day.
As vinegar is painful to the nose, so suffering that touches the body distresses the heart.
As a moth harms a garment and a worm harms wood, so a person's grief harms the heart.
If your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him a drink.
By doing this you will heap coals of fire on his head, and the Lord will reward you with good.
The north wind stirs up clouds, and a shameless face provokes a tongue.
It is better to live in a corner of the roof than in a shared house with a woman who hurls insults.
Like water to a thirsty soul is good news from a distant land.
Like someone who blocks a spring and ruins the outflow of its water, so it is unseemly for a righteous person to fall before an ungodly one.
It is not good to eat a great deal of honey, but it is fitting to honour glorious words.
Like a city whose wall is broken down and that has no wall, so is a man who does anything without counsel.
Like dew at threshing time and rain at harvest, so honour does not suit a fool.
As birds and the starling fly away, so an empty curse will come upon no one.
A whip for the horse and a goad for the donkey, and a rod for a foolish people.
Do not answer a fool according to his folly, so that you do not become like him.
Do not answer a fool according to his folly, so that he does not think himself wise.
Whoever sends a fool as a messenger to carry a word brings reproach on himself through his own ways.
Cut off the walking of the feet, and the proverbs from the mouth of a fool.
Like someone who puts a stone in a sling is the one who gives glory to a fool.
A thorn springs up in the hand of a drunkard, and slavery in the hands of fools,
for their frenzy is crushed.
As a dog, when it returns to its own vomit, becomes loathsome, so too is the fool when, through his own wickedness, he returns to sin.
I saw a man who thought himself wise, but a fool had more hope than he.
The sluggard says, when he is sent out on the road: "There is a lion on the roads and murderers in the streets."
As a door turns on its hinge, so does the sluggard on his bed.
The sluggard has hidden his hands in his bosom and cannot bring them to his mouth.
The sluggard thinks himself wiser than one who brings back tidings in full.
Like one who seizes a dog by the tail is one who sets himself over another's lawsuit.
Just as those who are being healed throw out words before people, and whoever answers a word is the first to stumble,
so too are those who lie in wait for their friends: when they are found out, they say, "We did this in jest."
With much wood a fire blazes up, and where there is an angry man, strife does not cease; but where there is no angry man, strife is always at rest.
A hearth is for coals, wood is for fire, and a reviling man is for turmoil and strife.
The words of the cut-tailed ones are soft [?]; these strike the treasure-chambers of the belly.
Silver given with deceit is counted as a potsherd, and smooth lips cover a grieving heart.
With his lips an enemy, weeping, assents to everything, but in his heart he contrives deceit with evil words.
However much an enemy entreats you earnestly [?] with a loud voice, do not believe him, for there are seven wickednesses in his heart.
Whoever hides enmity gathers deceit; he covers his sins openly in the assembly.
Whoever digs a pit for his neighbour will fall into it himself, and whoever rolls a stone rolls it onto his own head.
A lying tongue hates the truth, and the mouth of an unrestrained man stirs up turmoil.
Do not boast about tomorrow, for you do not know what the coming day will bring forth.
Let your neighbour praise you, and not your own mouth; strangers, and not your own lips.
A stone is heavy and sand is hard to carry, but a fool's wrath is heavier than both.
Anger is merciless and wrath is sharp, but nothing is more hideous than they [?] — jealousy.
Open rebukes are better than those of hidden love.
The wounds of a friend are more worthy of trust than the willing kisses of an enemy.
A well-fed soul scorns a honeycomb, but to a needy soul even what is bitter seems sweet.
Like a bird when it flies up from its nest, so is a man when he becomes a stranger to his own places.
He is a slave. The heart delights in ointments and wines and incense, but the soul is cast down by misfortunes.
Do not abandon your friend or your father's friend, and do not go into your brother's house without being asked. A friend who is near is better than a brother who is far away.
Be wise, my son, so that your heart may rejoice, and turn reproachful words away from yourself.
The prudent man hid himself when evil came, but the foolish went on into it and paid the penalty.
Take his garment, for his reviler has gone by, the one who ruins what belongs to another.
Whoever blesses a friend early in the morning with a loud voice will be no different from one who curses.
Dripping drives a man out on winter days, and in the same way a reviling woman drives a man out of his own house.
The fierce wind from above is called by the name "right-hand".
Iron sharpens iron, and a man provokes his friend's face to anger.
Whoever plants a fig tree will eat its fruit; whoever guards his master will find honor.
Just as one face is not like another face, so men's hearts are not like one another.
Hell and destruction can never be filled, and in the same way men's eyes can never be filled.
Abhorrent to the Lord is the one who fixes his eyes, and so are the uninstructed with their unrestrained tongues.
Silver and gold are tested by burning, but a man is tested by the mouth of the one who praises him.
The heart of the lawless seeks out evil, but the heart of the upright seeks out knowledge.
If you punish a fool in the middle of the assembly and rebuke him, you will still not rid him of his folly.
Know the souls of your flock well, and give your heart to your herds.
For a man's strength and power do not last forever, and they are not handed down from generation to generation.
Take care of the green grass in the field, mow the meadow, and gather the hay from the green grass,
so that you may have sheep for clothing. Honor the field, so that you may have lambs.
My son, you have from me mighty words for your life and for the life of your servants.
The ungodly man runs away when no one is chasing him, but the righteous man is as confident as a lion.
Through the sins of the ungodly [strife] arises, but a prudent man will quench it.
A man in his ungodliness slanders the poor, like a fierce and useless rain.
Those who abandon the law praise the ungodly, but those who love the law set it as a wall around themselves.
Wicked men do not understand justice, but those who seek the Lord will find it.
In every way a poor man who walks in truth is better than a rich man who lies.
A wise son keeps the law, but one who pursues impurity dishonors his father.
Whoever increases his wealth by usury and interest gathers it for the one who is merciful to the poor.
Whoever turns his ear away from hearing the law, even his prayer is detestable.
Whoever leads the upright astray onto an evil way will himself be given over to destruction; and the lawless pass by what is good and do not enter into it.
A rich man seems wise in his own eyes, but a poor man with understanding will judge him for what he is.
Through the help of the righteous great glory comes about, but in the places of the ungodly men are destroyed.
Whoever hides his ungodliness will not prosper, but whoever confesses it will be loved.
Blessed is the man who fears in all things out of reverence for God, but the hard-hearted man will fall into evil.
Like a hungry lion and a thirsty wolf is one who [?] rules over a nation of the poor.
A king short of revenue is a great slanderer, but the man who hates falsehood will live a long time.
Whoever bears the guilt of murder will be a fugitive and not secure.
Train your son, and he will give you rest and will bring adornment to your soul, and he will not obey a lawless nation.
Whoever walks justly will receive help, but whoever walks in crooked ways will be caught in them.
Whoever works his own land will be filled with bread, but whoever chases idleness will be filled with poverty.
A worthy man who acts faithfully will be greatly blessed, but one who does evil will not go unpunished.
It is not good when people are ashamed to rebuke liars to their faces; such a man will betray a person for a morsel of bread.
An envious man hurries to get rich and does not know that a merciful man will take possession of it.
Whoever rebukes a man for his ways will win more favor than one who flatters with his tongue.
Whoever does violence to father or mother and thinks he is not sinning is a partner of the ungodly man.
A dissolute man judges in vain.
Whoever trusts in the hardness of his own heart is a fool, but whoever trusts in the Lord will be in diligent striving. And whoever walks in wisdom will be saved.
Whoever gives to the poor will not be in want, but whoever turns his face away from the poor will be in great poverty.
In the place of the ungodly the righteous groan, but at their destruction the righteous will multiply.
Better is a man who rebukes a stiff-necked man; when he suddenly flares up there will be no healing.
At the praise of the righteous the peoples will rejoice, but under the rule of the ungodly people groan.
When a man loves wisdom, his father rejoices; but whoever keeps company with prostitutes will waste his wealth.
A righteous king raises up the land, but a lawless man overthrows it.
