Whoever sets about flattering his friend to his face lays a snare for his own feet.
A man's sin is a great snare, but the righteous will be in joy and gladness.
The righteous knows the cause of the poor, but the ungodly will not understand knowledge, and the poor man has no mind for knowledge.
Lawless men set the city on fire, but the wise turned away wrath.
A righteous man judges the nations, but a foolish man, when he is angry, is reproached and is not ashamed.
Bloodthirsty men hate a holy man, but the upright seek out his soul.
A fool pours out all his anger, but the wise man stores it up little by little.
When a king listens to lying words, all those who serve him are liars.
The lender and the borrower meet each other; the Lord watches over them both.
A righteous king who judges the poor with truth: his throne will be established as a witness.
Blows and rebukes give wisdom, but a child who goes astray brings shame on his father and mother.
When the ungodly are many, sins become many, but the righteous are afraid at their fall.
Instruct your son, and he will give you rest and bring adornment to your soul.
And he will not be one who tells things to a lawless nation; but whoever guards himself against the lawless is blessed.
A stubborn servant will not be instructed by words; even if he understands, he will not obey.
If you see a man who is hasty in his words, know that there is more hope for a fool than for him.
Whoever lives in luxury from his youth will become a slave, and in the end he will lament over himself.
An angry man digs up victory [?] for himself, but a wrathful man digs up sin.
Reviling brings a man low, but the Lord upholds the lowly with glory.
Whoever shares with a thief hates his own soul. If an oath is put forward among them and they do not tell,
those who fear and are not ashamed before men stumble. But whoever trusts in the Lord will rejoice. Ungodliness brings a stumbling-block upon a man, but whoever trusts in the Lord will be saved.
Many serve the face of rulers, but a man's justice comes from the Lord.
A righteous man is an abomination to a sinful man, and those whose way is made straight are an abomination to the lawless.
My son, fear my words, keep them, and repent. This is what the man says to those who believe in God: and I fall silent.
I am more foolish than all men, and the understanding of men is not in me.
God has taught me wisdom, and I have come to know the knowledge of the holy ones.

Who has gone up to heaven and come down? Or who has gathered the winds in his bosom? Or who has gathered the waters in a garment? Who has taken hold of the ends of the earth? What is his name? Or what is the name of his son?
For all the words of God are refined in the fire, and he helps those who fear him.
Do not add to his words, so that he does not rebuke you and you are not shown to be a liar.
Therefore I ask of you: do not take it away from me until I die.
Put vain words and lies far from me. Do not give me riches or poverty, but appoint for me what is fitting, so that I lack nothing,
so that I do not become full and turn liar and say, "Who sees me?", or become poor and steal and swear by the name of my God.
Do not hand a servant over into the hands of his master, or he may curse you and you will be ruined.
A wicked offspring curses his father and does not bless his mother.
A wicked offspring declares himself righteous and does not wash away his own filth (literally, "his going-out").
A wicked offspring has haughty eyes and lifts himself up with his eyelids.
A wicked offspring has teeth like swords and molars that cut, to devour and eat up the lowly from the earth and its poor from among men.
The leech had three daughters, dearly loved. Those three could not satisfy her, and the fourth could not bring herself to say, "Enough":
Hell, and the love of women, and Tartarus, and the earth that is not filled with water; and water and fire do not say, "Enough."
The eyes that mock a father and scorn the old age of a mother: may the ravens of the valley pluck them out and the young eagles devour them.
There are three things that I cannot know, and the fourth I do not understand:
the track of a flying eagle, the path of a snake on a rock, the place of a sunken ship, and the ways of a man in his youth.
Such is the way of an adulterous woman: when she has done it, she says, "I have done nothing wrong."
Three things make the earth shake, and the fourth it cannot bear:
when a slave becomes king, and when a fool is filled with bread;
and when a maidservant drives out her own mistress, and when a hateful woman gets a good husband.
Four things are the smallest on the earth, and they are wiser than the wise.
Among them are the ants, which have no strength, yet they prepare their food in summer.
And the badgers, a feeble race, which make their nests in the rock.
The locust has no king, yet it is trained to march in good order at a single command.
And the lizard [?] holds fast to the rock with its hands. Though it is easily caught, it lives in royal palaces.
There are three that walk well, and a fourth that goes along well:
the lion's whelp, the strongest of beasts, which does not turn back and is not terrified by any wild animal;
and the cock, which moves about among the hens without straying from them and without resting; and the he-goat, the leader of the flocks; and the king who calls out to the nations.
If you give yourself up to merriment and put your hand to your mouth in strife, you will be disgraced.
Milk is churned and becomes butter. If you squeeze the nose, blood comes out. If you draw out words, quarrels and lawsuits come out.
My words are spoken by God: the command of a king, whom his mother instructed.
What, son, is keeping the commandments of God? First of all I tell you, son: what is it, son of my womb? What is it, son of my prayers?
Do not give your wealth to women, and do not give your mind and your life to foolish counsel.
Do everything with counsel, and drink wine with counsel. The mighty are quick to anger; do not drink wine,
so that they do not drink and forget wisdom, and become unable to judge the weak rightly.
Strong drink is given to those who mourn, and wine to drink to those who suffer,
so that they forget their poverty and no longer remember their pain.
Open your mouth with the word of God, and judge everyone soundly.
Open your mouth and judge with righteousness; judge the cause of the poor and the weak.
Who can find a brave and capable woman? For such a woman is worth more than the most precious gems.
Her husband's heart trusts in her. Such a woman will lack no spoil,
for she helps her husband to do good all his life.
She got wool and flax and made useful things with her own hands.
And she became like a ship coming from far away. She gathered everything needed for living.
And she rises at night and gives food to her household, to the workers and to the maidservants.
She saw suitable land and bought it. From the fruits of her hands she planted a property.
And she girded her loins firmly and set her arms moving to work.
And she tasted and saw that the work is good; her lamp does not go out all night.
She put her hands to the distaff and stretched out her arms to what is better.
She opened her hands to the poor and stretched out her arm to the fallen.
Her husband has no worries about the house if he stays away anywhere; all who belong to her are clothed.
She made a double cloak for her husband; fine linen and purple are clothing for herself.
Her husband is admired at the gates when he sits in the assembly among the elders who live in the land.
She made robes and handed them out to the Phoenicians, and girdles to the Canaanites.
She opened her mouth with wisdom and set her tongue in order.
She clothed herself in strength and beauty, and she rejoiced in the last days.
The rooms of her house are dry; she did not eat the bread of idleness.
She opens her mouth with wisdom and according to the law. Her children rose up and praised her, and her husband also praised her:
"Many women have gained wealth, and many have done mighty things, but you have outdone and surpassed them all."
False charms and the empty beauty of women are not found in you, for a wise woman who serves well will be blessed. Those who fear the Lord praise her.
Give her some of the fruit of her lips, and let her husband be praised at the gates, for the ways of men went before her, and they were made straight for ever and ever.
